name: 93LC56B-I_SN
title: 93AA56, 93LC56 and 93C56 (A, B, C versions): 2 Kbit Microwire-compatible serial EEPROM
summary: A family of 2 Kbit serial EEPROMs on a three-wire Microwire-compatible bus (CS, CLK, DI and DO). The A parts are fixed at 256 x 8, the B parts at 128 x 16, and the C parts choose between the two with the ORG pin. 93AA56 runs from 1.8 V, 93LC56 from 2.5 V and 93C56 from 4.5 V, all up to 5.5 V; erase and write cycles are self-timed, DO reports ready or busy, and the part powers up write-disabled. 93LC56B-I/SN is the 16-bit 93LC56 in an 8-lead 3.90 mm SOIC rated -40°C to +85°C.
key_figures: 2 Kbit: 256 x 8 (A), 128 x 16 (B), either by ORG (C)
2 MHz max from 2.5 V; 1 MHz below 2.5 V; 3 MHz for 93XX56C at 4.5 V and up

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Chip select, active high. Low deselects the part and puts it in standby; a programming cycle already started still finishes. Must stay low at least TCSL (250 ns) between instructions; while it is low the internal logic stays reset.

pins.name: CLK
pins.function: Serial clock. Opcode, address and data are taken in, and read data shifted out, on the rising edge. May be stopped high or low at any point; ignored while CS is low.

pins.name: DI

pins.name: DO
pins.function: Serial data output. Drives read data TPD after each rising CLK edge; during an erase or write it shows ready (high) or busy (low). High impedance otherwise and once CS goes low.

operation.text: On 93XX56C, ORG tied to VCC selects 128 words of 16 bits and ORG tied to ground selects 256 words of 8 bits. 93XX56A is always x8 and 93XX56B always x16. The address field is 8 bits wide in x8 (A7-A0) and 7 bits in x16 (A6-A0).
DI is sampled on each rising CLK edge. DO stays high impedance except while read data is going out or while ready/busy status is being shown, and returns to high impedance when CS falls.

The first rising CLK edge that finds both CS and DI high is the start bit. Before it, CS, CLK and DI may move in any pattern other than a start condition and nothing happens. Raising CS takes the part out of standby. When CS goes high to begin an instruction, CLK or DI must be low.

An instruction runs only if every opcode, address and data bit it needs has been clocked in: 11 clocks in x16 and 12 in x8 for ERASE, ERAL, EWEN and EWDS; 27 (x16) or 20 (x8) for READ, WRITE and WRAL. After that CLK and DI are ignored until the next start bit. With CS high and no start bit yet (DI low), any number of clocks leave the part waiting. No clocks are needed during a self-timed erase or write.

DI and DO may share one wire, but when A0 is a 1 the dummy zero DO drives ahead of read data fights the source still driving A0, and the level seen is set by the two drive strengths. A resistor between DI and DO limits the current in that case.

All operations are blocked while VCC is below about 1.5 V (93AA, 93LC) or 3.8 V (93C). At power-up erase and write are disabled (EWDS), so EWEN must be sent before the first ERASE or WRITE. For further protection an EWDS after every write and a 10 kΩ pull-down on CS are recommended.
EWEN enables programming until EWDS is sent or power is removed; EWDS disables every erase and write function. READ works the same under either.

ERASE sets every bit of the addressed word to 1. On 93AA and 93LC parts the self-timed cycle starts when CS falls after the last address bit; on 93C parts it starts on the rising CLK edge ahead of the final address bit.

ERAL sets the whole array to 1. It is timed like ERASE with its own opcode; 93AA and 93LC start it on CS falling, 93C on the rising CLK edge ahead of the final data bit. No clocks are needed once it runs. ERAL needs VCC of 4.5 V or more; TEC is 6 ms max.

READ puts a dummy 0 on DO and then the 8-bit (x8) or 16-bit (x16) word, most significant bit first, each bit changing on a rising CLK edge and valid TPD later. Holding CS high and continuing to clock reads the following words in turn.

WRITE is followed by 8 (x8) or 16 (x16) data bits for the addressed word, and the word is erased automatically before it is written. On 93AA and 93LC parts the self-timed cycle starts when CS falls once the final data bit is in; on 93C parts on the rising CLK edge of the last data bit. TWC is 6 ms max (93AA, 93LC) or 2 ms max (93C).

WRAL writes the given data word into every location. It erases the array itself first, so no ERAL is needed, but EWEN must be in force. It starts like WRITE, needs no clocks once running, and needs VCC of 4.5 V or more; TWL is 15 ms max.

After an erase or write has started, taking CS low for at least TCSL (250 ns) and then high again shows status on DO within TSV: low while programming, high when done. If CS stays low for the whole cycle DO stays high impedance; checking after the cycle shows high. To clear the status from DO, send a start bit and then drop CS; standby current is specified with DO cleared.
Taking CS low during a programming cycle does not stop it; the part enters standby once the cycle is complete.
On DFN and TDFN the exposed pad may connect to VSS or float.
Rated for 1,000,000 erase/write cycles and data retention beyond 200 years. Lead-free and RoHS-compliant; leads are matte tin, and the MNY TDFN is NiPdAu.
